questions.text: एक योजनात्मक पॉलीन्यूक्लियोटाइड शृंखला में '–––––' लाइन इसके प्रकार बंध का निरूपण दर्शाती है :
questions.text_english: The type of bond represented by the dotted line '–––––' in a schematic polynucleotide chain is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Phosphodiester bond. In a polynucleotide chain, the backbone is formed by alternating sugar (S) and phosphate (P) groups. The dotted line shown in the diagram connects the sugar (S) to the nitrogenous base (B), which represents the N-glycosidic linkage — but if the dotted line in the figure connects successive nucleotides through the phosphate group between two sugars, it represents the phosphodiester bond. The phosphodiester bond links the 3' carbon of one deoxyribose sugar to the 5' carbon of the next via a phosphate group, forming the backbone of the polynucleotide chain. Hydrogen bonds occur between complementary bases of two strands, peptide bonds occur in proteins, and N-glycosidic linkage connects base to sugar within a nucleotide.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) फॉस्फोडाइएस्टर बंध है। पॉलीन्यूक्लियोटाइड श्रृंखला में फॉस्फोडाइएस्टर बंध एक न्यूक्लियोटाइड के 3' कार्बन को अगले न्यूक्लियोटाइड के 5' कार्बन से जोड़ता है।

questions.text: उस विकल्प को चुनिए जिसमें मानव मादा (स्त्री) के जनन चक्र की परिघटनाओं के सही अनुक्रम को दर्शाया गया है : (i) एफएसएच (FSH) का स्रवण (ii) अंडोत्सर्ग (iii) पीतपिंड का वर्धन (iv) पुटक का वर्धन तथा अंडजनन (v) एलएच (LH) स्तर में आकस्मिक वृद्धि
questions.text_english: Select the option that has the correct sequence of events of human female reproductive cycle : (i) Secretion of FSH (ii) Ovulation (iii) Growth of corpus luteum (iv) Growth of follicle and oogenesis (v) Sudden increase in LH
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) i–iv–v–ii–iii. The correct sequence of events in the human female menstrual cycle is: first, FSH is secreted by the anterior pituitary (i), which stimulates the growth of the follicle and oogenesis (iv). As the follicle matures, estrogen rises, triggering a sudden surge in LH levels (v), which causes ovulation — the release of the secondary oocyte (ii). After ovulation, the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum (iii), which secretes progesterone to maintain the uterine lining.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) i–iv–v–ii–iii है। मानव मादा के मासिक चक्र का सही क्रम: FSH स्रवण → पुटक वर्धन व अंडजनन → LH में आकस्मिक वृद्धि → अंडोत्सर्ग → पीतपिंड का वर्धन।

questions.text: दूध को दही में स्कंदित करने वाले लैक्टोबैसिलस को सामान्यत: इस वर्ग में रखते हैं :
questions.text_english: Lactobacillus that sets milk into curd is categorised as :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Heterotrophic bacteria. Lactobacillus is a heterotrophic bacterium because it cannot synthesise its own food and depends on organic matter (lactose in milk) for nutrition. It ferments lactose into lactic acid, which causes the milk to coagulate and form curd. Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic, archaebacteria are found in extreme environments, and chemosynthetic bacteria use inorganic compounds for energy — none of which describes Lactobacillus.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) विषमपोषी बैक्टीरिया है। लैक्टोबैसिलस अपना भोजन स्वयं नहीं बना सकता, यह दूध में उपस्थित लैक्टोज को लैक्टिक अम्ल में किण्वित करता है।

questions.text: विशिष्ट Bt जीव विष जींस जो कपास के पौधों को कपास गोलक शलभ कृमियों के प्रति सुरक्षा प्रदान करते हैं, वह जींस हैं :
questions.text_english: The specific Bt toxin genes which protect the cotton plants against the cotton bollworms are :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Cry-I Ac and Cry-II Ab. Bacillus thuringiensis produces Bt toxins encoded by cry genes. The specific cry genes that confer resistance to cotton bollworms in Bt cotton are Cry-I Ac and Cry-II Ab. These genes produce proteins that form pores in the midgut of the bollworm larvae, causing their death. Other cry genes like Cry-I Ab target different pests such as corn borer.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) Cry-I Ac और Cry-II Ab है। ये जींस कपास के पौधों को कपास गोलक शलभ कृमियों से बचाते हैं।

questions.text: नीचे दी गई तालिका में कुछ ऐमीनो अम्ल तथा उनसे संबंधित एमआरएनए कोडॉन दिए गए हैं : फेनिलएलेनीन – UUU, लाइसीन – AAG, आर्जिनीन – CGA, एलेनीन – GCA। उस डीएनए अनुक्रम का चयन कीजिए जो निम्नलिखित पॉलीपेप्टाइड अनुक्रम का कोड निर्धारित करेगा : पॉलिपेप्टाइड : एलेनीन – आर्जिनीन – लाइसीन – फेनिलएलेनीन
questions.text_english: Listed below are some amino acids and their corresponding mRNA codons: Phenylalanine – UUU, Lysine – AAG, Arginine – CGA, Alanine – GCA. Select the DNA sequence that would code for the following polypeptide sequence: Polypeptide: Alanine – Arginine – Lysine – Phenylalanine
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) CGT GCT TTC AAA. To find the DNA coding strand, we take the complement of the mRNA codons and replace U with T. Alanine mRNA codon is GCA → DNA coding strand is CGT. Arginine mRNA codon is CGA → DNA coding strand is GCT. Lysine mRNA codon is AAG → DNA coding strand is TTC. Phenylalanine mRNA codon is UUU → DNA coding strand is AAA. DNA uses T (thymine) not U (uracil), so options C and D (which contain U) are incorrect as they represent RNA, not DNA sequences.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) CGT GCT TTC AAA है। mRNA कोडॉन का DNA कोडिंग स्ट्रैंड में परिवर्तन करते हुए U को T से बदला जाता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस पौधे में नर तथा मादा पुष्प दोनों एक ही पौधे पर पुष्पित होते हैं तथा उनमें सजातपुष्पी परागण अथवा परनिषेचन संभव है ?
questions.text_english: In which of the following plants are both male and female flowers born on the same plant and the mode of pollination can be geitonogamy or xenogamy ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Maize. Maize (Zea mays) is a monoecious plant, meaning both male (tassel) and female (silk/cob) flowers are borne on the same plant. Since the flowers are spatially separated on the same plant, pollination can occur between flowers of the same plant (geitonogamy) or between flowers of different plants (xenogamy). Papaya and Date Palm are dioecious (male and female flowers on different plants), and Spinach is also typically dioecious.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) मक्का है। मक्का एकलिंगाश्रयी पौधा है जिसमें नर और मादा दोनों पुष्प एक ही पौधे पर होते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पारजीवी जंतुओं (ट्रांसजेनिक एनिमल्स) में से किसे पोलियो के टीके (वैक्सीन) की सुरक्षा परीक्षण हेतु उपयोग किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following transgenic animals is being used to test the safety of the polio vaccine ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Mice. Transgenic mice have been developed that express the human poliovirus receptor. These transgenic mice are used to test the safety and efficacy of the polio vaccine because they are susceptible to poliovirus infection in a way similar to humans. This reduces the need for experiments on primates and provides a more reliable animal model for vaccine safety testing.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) चूहा है। ट्रांसजेनिक चूहों में मानव पोलियोवायरस रिसेप्टर व्यक्त होता है, इसलिए इनका उपयोग पोलियो वैक्सीन की सुरक्षा परीक्षण हेतु किया जाता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किस प्रकार की परिस्थितियों/रोग में मानव शरीर में मास्ट कोशिकाओं की अतिक्रियाशीलता (में वृद्धि) प्रेक्षित होती है ?
questions.text_english: In which of the following conditions/diseases is there a substantial increase in the activity of mast cells observed in the human body ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Allergy. Mast cells are tissue-resident immune cells that play a central role in allergic reactions. During an allergic response, IgE antibodies produced against harmless allergens bind to receptors on mast cells. When the allergen is encountered again, it cross-links these IgE antibodies, causing mast cells to degranulate and release inflammatory chemicals like histamine, serotonin, and leukotrienes. These chemicals cause symptoms such as sneezing, watery eyes, and itching. Typhoid is caused by bacteria, ascariasis by parasitic worms, and AIDS involves destruction of T-helper cells — none involve mast cell hyperactivity.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) ऐलर्जी है। एलर्जी में IgE एंटीबॉडी मास्ट कोशिकाओं पर बंध जाते हैं और एलर्जन के पुनः संपर्क पर हिस्टामीन आदि रसायन मुक्त होते हैं।

questions.text: परिवार नियोजन हेतु किसी दम्पति द्वारा अपनाई जाने वाली आवधिक संयम अवधि होनी चाहिए :
questions.text_english: The periodic abstinence by a couple for family planning should be from :

options.A: माहवारी चक्र के 5वें से 10वें दिन के बीच
options.B: माहवारी चक्र के 13वें से 15वें दिन के बीच
options.C: माहवारी चक्र के 10वें से 17वें दिन के बीच
options.D: माहवारी चक्र के 16वें से 20वें दिन के बीच

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Day 10 to 17 of menstrual cycle. In a 28-day menstrual cycle, ovulation typically occurs around day 14. The ovum can be fertilised for about 24 hours after ovulation, and sperm can survive for 2–3 days in the female reproductive tract. Therefore, the fertile period extends roughly from day 10 to day 17. Couples practising the rhythm method or periodic abstinence avoid sexual intercourse during this period to prevent pregnancy.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) माहवारी चक्र के 10वें से 17वें दिन के बीच है। इस अवधि में अंडोत्सर्ग होता है और गर्भधारण की संभावना सर्वाधिक होती है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित से गलत जोड़े का चयन कीजिए : मानव कैरियोटाइप – लक्षण : (A) 45+XX – चौड़ी हथेली में अभिलाक्षणिक पाम क्रीज़, (B) 44+XXY – समग्र रूप से मादा लक्षण का विकास, (C) 44+XO – अल्पवर्धित अंडाशय के कारण नारी बाँझ होती है, (D) 44+XY – सामान्य नर (पुरुष)
questions.text_english: Select the incorrect match from the following: Human Karyotype – Characters: (A) 45+XX – Broad palm with characteristic palm crease, (B) 44+XXY – Overall feminine development, (C) 44+XO – Sterile females as ovaries are rudimentary, (D) 44+XY – Normal male
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 45+XX. The karyotype with broad palm and characteristic palm crease (simian crease) is associated with Down's syndrome, which has a total of 47 chromosomes (44+XY or 44+XX, i.e., trisomy 21), not 45+XX. The 45+XX description actually refers to a normal female (44 autosomes + 2 X chromosomes). The 44+XXY (total 47) is Klinefelter's syndrome showing overall feminine features. 44+XO (total 45) is Turner's syndrome with rudimentary ovaries and sterility. 44+XY is a normal male.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) 45+XX है। चौड़ी हथेली व पाम क्रीज़ डाउन सिंड्रोम (ट्राइसॉमी 21) का लक्षण है, न कि 45+XX का।

questions.text: डीएनए टेम्पलेट का उपयोग करके पीसीआर प्रवर्धन में 10 चक्रों के उपरांत कितने नए डीएनए अणु निर्मित (जनित) होंगे ?
questions.text_english: Using a DNA template, how many new DNA molecules would be generated after 10 cycles of amplification in PCR ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 1024. In PCR, each cycle doubles the number of DNA molecules. Starting with 1 DNA template, after n cycles the total number of DNA molecules is 2^n. After 10 cycles, the total number of DNA molecules = 2^10 = 1024. Therefore, the number of new DNA molecules generated (excluding the original template) would be 1024 – 1 = 1023, but since the question asks for total molecules generated after 10 cycles, the answer is 1024.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 1024 है। PCR में प्रत्येक चक्र DNA की संख्या दोगुनी करता है। 10 चक्रों के बाद 2^10 = 1024 DNA अणु बनते हैं।

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए चार वक्तव्यों को पढ़िए तथा दो सही वक्तव्यों वाले विकल्प को चुनिए : (i) एक हिरण को खाने वाला शेर तथा खाद्यान्न को खाने वाली गौरैया पारिस्थितिकी के अनुसार उपभोक्ता होने के कारण सदृश हैं। (ii) परभक्षी तारामीन पाइसैस्टर कुछ अकशेरुकियों की जातीय विविधता का अनुरक्षण करने में सहायक है। (iii) परभक्षी अंतत: शिकार जातियों का विलोपन कर देते हैं। (iv) पौधों द्वारा निकोटीन तथा स्ट्रीचनीन रसायनों का निर्माण उपापचयी विकार हैं।
questions.text_english: Read the four statements given below and select the option having two correct statements: (i) A lion eating a deer and a sparrow feeding on grains are ecologically similar in being consumers. (ii) Predator starfish Pisaster helps in maintaining species diversity of some invertebrates. (iii) Predators ultimately lead to extinction of prey species. (iv) Production of chemicals nicotine and strychnine by plants are metabolic disorders.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (i) and (ii). Statement (i) is correct — both a lion eating a deer and a sparrow eating grains are consumers as they depend on other organisms for food; they occupy different trophic levels but are both consumers ecologically. Statement (ii) is correct — the predatory starfish Pisaster prevents mussels from competitively excluding other invertebrates, thereby maintaining biodiversity. Statement (iii) is incorrect — predators do not normally cause extinction of prey; in fact, they regulate prey populations, keeping ecosystems balanced. Statement (iv) is incorrect — nicotine and strychnine are not metabolic disorders but are defensive chemicals (secondary metabolites) produced by plants to deter herbivores.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) (i) और (ii) है। शेर और गौरैया दोनों उपभोक्ता हैं, और पाइसैस्टर तारामीन जातीय विविधता बनाए रखता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : एग्रोबैक्टीरियम ट्यूमेफेशियन्स अनेक एकबीजपत्री पौधों का रोगकारक है।
कारण (R) : पौधे में प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं को ट्यूमर में रूपांतरित करने हेतु यह डीएनए के एक अंश 'T-डीएनए' को हस्तांतरित करने में समर्थ है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of several monocot plants.
Reason (R): It is able to deliver a piece of DNA known as 'T-DNA' to transform normal plant cells into a tumor.
questions.instruction_line: For Questions 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).
questions.instruction_line_english: For Questions 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) — Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true. The assertion is incorrect because Agrobacterium tumefaciens is a pathogen of dicot plants, not monocot plants. It causes crown gall disease in dicots. The reason is correct: Agrobacterium tumefaciens does transfer a segment of DNA called T-DNA (tumour-inducing DNA) from its Ti plasmid into the plant cell nucleus, where it integrates into the plant genome and transforms normal plant cells into tumour cells.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। अभिकथन गलत है क्योंकि एग्रोबैक्टीरियम द्विबीजपत्री पौधों का रोगकारक है, न कि एकबीजपत्री का। कारण सही है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : हमारे देश का कानून शिशु को कानूनन गोद लेने की इजाज़त देता है और यह आज भी संतानविहीन दंपति के लिए जनकता प्राप्ति का सर्वोत्तम उपाय है।
कारण (R) : भारत में अनाथ और दीन-हीन बच्चों को कानूनी रूप से गोद लेने में भावनात्मक, धार्मिक तथा सामाजिक घटक बाधक नहीं हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The laws of our country permit legal adoption and it is as yet, one of the best methods for childless couples looking for parenthood.
Reason (R): Emotional, religious and social factors are no deterrents to the legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children in India.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. The assertion is correct: Indian law does permit legal adoption and it is indeed one of the best natural ways for childless couples to experience parenthood. However, the reason is false: in reality, emotional, religious, and social factors do act as significant deterrents to adoption in India. Many families prefer biological children and social stigmas around adoption remain widespread, which is why adoption rates remain low despite legal provisions.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) — Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion. Linked genes are located on the same chromosome. Because they are physically connected, they tend to be inherited together and do not segregate independently during meiosis. This violates Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, which applies only to genes located on different (non-homologous) chromosomes. As a result, linked genes do not produce the expected 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratio in F2; instead, parental combinations are more frequent than recombinant types.

questions.text_english: Do you think apomixis can be compared to asexual reproduction ? Justify your answer. State the benefits of apomixis to the farmers.

key_points: Yes, apomixis can be compared to asexual reproduction because seeds are produced without fertilisation.
In apomixis, the embryo develops from the diploid egg cell or nucellus without meiosis or syngamy.
Benefit 1: Farmers can save hybrid seeds year after year without loss of hybrid vigour.
Benefit 2: It helps in the production of seeds that are true to type, maintaining desirable traits.

questions.solution: Yes, apomixis can be compared to asexual reproduction because in both processes new individuals are produced without the fusion of gametes (fertilisation). In apomixis, seeds are formed from the diploid egg cell or from the cells of the nucellus without meiosis, so the offspring are genetically identical to the parent — exactly as in asexual reproduction. The main benefit of apomixis to farmers is that it allows hybrid seed production without repeated crossing each season. Farmers can save and replant hybrid seeds year after year and the plants will maintain the same high-yielding, disease-resistant characters without loss of hybrid vigour (heterosis).

sub_questions.solution: Organic farmers do not recommend complete eradication of insect pests because they depend on biological control for pest management. They introduce or encourage natural enemies of pests — such as parasitoid wasps, predatory beetles, and other beneficial insects — to control pest populations. If all pests are eliminated, these beneficial predators and parasitoids would lose their food source and their populations would collapse. Without natural biological control agents, any future pest outbreak would be uncontrollable. Hence, maintaining a small pest population is necessary to sustain the biological control system.

key_points: The naturalist is Charles Darwin (or Jean-Baptiste Lamarck if the picture depicts use-and-disuse).
The picture shows giraffes with gradually elongating necks, which Darwin used to explain natural selection.
Explanation: Giraffes with longer necks could reach higher leaves and had better chances of survival and reproduction; over generations, natural selection favoured longer-necked individuals.

questions.solution: The naturalist depicted is Jean-Baptiste Lamarck (if the figure shows gradual neck elongation due to stretching). According to Lamarck's theory of inheritance of acquired characters, ancestral giraffes had short necks. They stretched their necks to reach leaves on tall trees, and this repeated use caused the neck to elongate. This acquired characteristic of a longer neck was then passed on to offspring. Over many generations, giraffes developed very long necks. However, if the question refers to Darwin's explanation: giraffes with naturally longer necks had a survival advantage in reaching food, were more fit, survived and reproduced more, passing on the long-neck trait — this is natural selection.

questions.text_english: Write the basic steps followed in the Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) programme to help childless couples. Why is it also known as test tube baby programme ?

key_points: Step 1: Eggs are collected from the wife/donor after hormonal stimulation.
Step 2: Sperm is collected from the husband/donor.
Step 3: Fertilisation is carried out outside the body (in vitro) in a laboratory.
Step 4: The zygote or early embryo is transferred into the uterus of the woman (IVF-ET).
It is called test tube baby programme because fertilisation takes place in a glass vessel (test tube) in the laboratory, outside the mother's body.

questions.solution: In the ART programme, the basic steps are: first, the woman is given hormonal treatment to stimulate superovulation so that multiple eggs are produced; the eggs are then collected surgically. Simultaneously, semen is collected from the male partner. Fertilisation is carried out outside the body in a laboratory dish — this in vitro fertilisation (IVF) produces a zygote. The zygote is allowed to develop into an 8-celled embryo and is then transferred into the uterus of the woman (embryo transfer, ET) where it implants and develops normally. It is called the test tube baby programme because fertilisation does not occur inside the mother's body but in a laboratory glass vessel, though the embryo develops inside the mother's womb.

sub_questions.text_english: What are transgenic animals ?

key_points: Animals that have had a piece of foreign DNA (a gene from another organism) experimentally introduced into their genome are called transgenic animals.

sub_questions.solution: Transgenic animals are animals whose DNA has been altered by the introduction of a foreign gene (a gene from another organism) into their genome using genetic engineering techniques. These animals express the foreign gene and can serve as models for human diseases, bioreactors for producing useful proteins, or subjects for vaccine safety testing.

key_points: Rosie was the first transgenic cow.
Rosie produced human protein-enriched milk (human alpha-lactalbumin) which is nutritionally more balanced for human infants than normal cow's milk.

sub_questions.solution: The first transgenic cow was Rosie. It was produced by inserting the human alpha-lactalbumin gene into its genome. As a result, Rosie produced milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin, making the milk nutritionally more suitable and balanced for human infants. This milk has a higher protein content than normal cow's milk and is closer in composition to human breast milk.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the convention for naming EcoRI.

key_points: 'E' stands for the genus Escherichia, 'co' for the species coli, 'R' for the strain RY13, and 'I' indicates it was the first restriction enzyme isolated from this strain.

sub_questions.solution: The naming convention for restriction enzymes uses the following system: the first letter is capitalised and refers to the genus of the organism from which the enzyme is isolated — 'E' stands for Escherichia. The next two letters (in lowercase) refer to the species — 'co' stands for coli. The letter 'R' identifies the strain of the organism — here, strain RY13. The Roman numeral 'I' indicates that this was the first restriction enzyme isolated from that particular strain. Thus, EcoRI means the first restriction enzyme from Escherichia coli strain RY13.

sub_questions.solution: EcoRI recognises the palindromic sequence 5'-G↓AATTC-3' on the DNA double helix and cuts between G and A on both strands, creating 4-nucleotide 5'-AATT single-stranded overhangs called 'sticky ends'. The diagram should show the double-stranded DNA with the recognition site, arrows indicating cut positions, and the two resulting fragments with staggered sticky ends.

questions.text_english: Explain the mode of action of contraceptive pills taken by human females. Mention the schedule to be followed for effective outcome.

key_points: Contraceptive pills contain synthetic progesterone (progestins) alone or combined with estrogen.
They inhibit ovulation by suppressing FSH and LH secretion from the pituitary.
They also cause thickening of cervical mucus, preventing sperm entry, and alter uterine lining, preventing implantation.
Schedule: One pill daily for 21 days starting within 5 days of the menstrual cycle; a gap of 7 days, then repeat.

questions.solution: Contraceptive pills contain synthetic forms of female sex hormones — progestins (synthetic progesterone) alone or in combination with estrogen. Their primary mode of action is to inhibit ovulation by suppressing the release of FSH and LH from the anterior pituitary through negative feedback. Without the LH surge, ovulation does not occur. Additionally, these hormones thicken the cervical mucus, which prevents sperm from entering the uterus, and alter the endometrial lining, making it unsuitable for implantation. The schedule to be followed is: one pill must be taken daily for 21 consecutive days, ideally starting within the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle. After 21 days, a 7-day gap is observed (during which withdrawal bleeding occurs), and then the cycle is repeated.

sub_questions.text_english: Name and write two characteristics of the type of DNA that forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting technique.

key_points: Satellite DNA (or VNTRs — Variable Number of Tandem Repeats) forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting.
Characteristic 1: It is highly polymorphic — the number of repeat units varies significantly between individuals.
Characteristic 2: It shows the same degree of polymorphism whether obtained from blood, hair, saliva, or any other tissue of the same individual.

sub_questions.solution: The type of DNA that forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting is Satellite DNA, specifically Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs) or microsatellites. Its two key characteristics are: first, it is highly polymorphic — the number of repeat units at a given locus varies greatly from person to person, making each individual's DNA pattern unique (except in identical twins). Second, the pattern is tissue-independent — whether DNA is extracted from blood, hair roots, saliva, or skin, the VNTR pattern remains the same for the same individual.

sub_questions.text: इस तकनीक के कोई दो अनुप्रयोगों का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two applications of this technique.

key_points: 1. Forensic science: identification of criminals or victims from biological samples left at crime scenes.
2. Paternity testing: to determine the biological father or mother of a child in disputed cases.

sub_questions.solution: Two important applications of DNA fingerprinting are: first, it is used extensively in forensic science to identify suspects or victims in criminal investigations by matching DNA from blood stains, hair, or other biological material found at crime scenes with that of suspected individuals. Second, it is used in paternity and maternity disputes to determine the biological parentage of a child, since a child's DNA pattern is a combination of both parents' VNTR patterns.

key_points: Satellite DNA (VNTRs); highly polymorphic; tissue-independent pattern. Applications: forensic identification, paternity testing.

questions.solution: The DNA forming the basis of DNA fingerprinting is Satellite DNA (VNTRs — Variable Number of Tandem Repeats). It is highly polymorphic (unique to each individual) and shows the same banding pattern regardless of which tissue of the same individual is analysed. Two applications are: (1) forensic identification of criminals or victims from biological evidence at crime scenes, and (2) determining biological parentage in paternity/maternity disputes.

sub_questions.text: रुधिर आलेप द्वारा निर्दशित रोग का नाम लिखिए । इस रोग के अभिलक्षण तथा कारण लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the disease the blood smear is indicative of. Write the symptoms of the disease and its cause.

key_points: Disease: Sickle Cell Anaemia
Cause: A single base substitution (GAG to GTG) in the beta-globin gene, resulting in glutamic acid being replaced by valine.
Symptoms: Sickle-shaped RBCs, anaemia, joint pain, fatigue, repeated infections.

sub_questions.solution: The blood smear is indicative of Sickle Cell Anaemia. The disease is caused by a point mutation — a single nucleotide substitution (A to T) — in the beta-globin gene of haemoglobin, changing codon GAG to GTG. This substitutes the amino acid glutamic acid with valine, producing abnormal haemoglobin (HbS). Under low oxygen conditions, HbS polymerises, causing RBCs to become sickle-shaped. Symptoms include chronic haemolytic anaemia (destruction of sickle-shaped RBCs), severe joint pain, fatigue, breathlessness, and increased susceptibility to infections.

sub_questions.text: समुचित क्रॉस की सहायता से रोग (विकार) के वंशागति पैटर्न की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the inheritance pattern of the disease with the help of a suitable cross.

key_points: Sickle cell anaemia follows autosomal recessive inheritance.
When two carriers (HbA HbS × HbA HbS) mate, the offspring ratio is 1 normal : 2 carriers : 1 affected.
Only homozygous individuals (HbS HbS) show the disease.

sub_questions.solution: Sickle cell anaemia is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. When two carriers (heterozygous individuals, HbA HbS) marry each other, the possible offspring are: 25% normal (HbA HbA), 50% carriers (HbA HbS) — who are phenotypically normal but carry the sickle cell allele, and 25% affected (HbS HbS) — who express full sickle cell disease. The cross is: HbA HbS × HbA HbS → 1 HbA HbA : 2 HbA HbS : 1 HbS HbS. Only HbS HbS individuals suffer from the disease.

key_points: Sickle Cell Anaemia; autosomal recessive; caused by point mutation in beta-globin gene.

questions.solution: The blood smear shows Sickle Cell Anaemia. It is inherited as autosomal recessive: cross HbA HbS × HbA HbS gives 1 normal : 2 carrier : 1 affected offspring.

sub_questions.text: एस.एल. मिलर द्वारा किए गए प्रयोग की साथर्कता की व्याख्या कीजिए तथा वैज्ञानिकों के नाम लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the significance of the experiment carried out by S.L. Miller and name the scientists whose hypothesis prompted it.

key_points: Miller simulated the conditions of early Earth (CH4, NH3, H2, H2O vapour, electric discharges) and showed that organic molecules (amino acids) could form abiotically.
This provided experimental support for the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis of chemical origin of life.
Scientists: A.I. Oparin and J.B.S. Haldane.

sub_questions.solution: S.L. Miller's experiment (1953) was significant because it demonstrated for the first time that organic molecules essential for life — specifically amino acids — could be synthesised abiotically from inorganic substances. Miller recreated the conditions of the primitive Earth atmosphere by combining methane (CH4), ammonia (NH3), hydrogen (H2), and water vapour in a closed flask and passing electric discharges (simulating lightning) through them. After a week, he found that amino acids such as glycine, alanine, and aspartic acid had formed. This experiment provided the first experimental evidence supporting the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis. The scientists who proposed this hypothesis were A.I. Oparin (Russian) and J.B.S. Haldane (British).

sub_questions.text_english: How does meteorite analysis favour this hypothesis ?

key_points: Analysis of meteorites has revealed the presence of amino acids and other organic molecules, suggesting that organic molecules can form abiotically in space, supporting the idea that life's building blocks can arise without living organisms.

sub_questions.solution: Analysis of meteorites (particularly carbonaceous chondrites) has revealed the presence of amino acids and other organic compounds. The discovery of the same amino acids that Miller synthesised in his experiment within meteorites provides independent evidence that organic molecules can form abiotically outside the Earth as well, strongly supporting the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis that life's chemical building blocks arose spontaneously from inorganic matter.

key_points: Miller's experiment showed abiotic synthesis of amino acids; Oparin and Haldane proposed the hypothesis; meteorite analysis found amino acids supporting abiotic origin.

questions.solution: Miller's experiment demonstrated that amino acids could be synthesised abiotically under simulated primitive Earth conditions (CH4, NH3, H2, H2O with electric sparks), supporting Oparin and Haldane's hypothesis of chemical evolution of life. Meteorite analysis supports this hypothesis because amino acids identical to those synthesised by Miller have been found in meteorites, confirming that organic molecules can arise abiotically.

questions.text_english: (a) State what is primary productivity and mention its units. (b) Some ecologists observed that primary productivity of a place in Rajasthan was low as compared to a particular place in Kerala. Explain why.

sub_questions.text: प्राथमिक उत्पादकता क्या है तथा इसे किस रूप (इकाई) में व्यक्त किया जाता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: State what is primary productivity and mention its units.

key_points: Primary productivity is the rate of biomass production (organic matter/energy) by producers (autotrophs) per unit area per unit time through photosynthesis.
It is expressed as grams of dry weight per square metre per year (g dry wt m-2 yr-1) or kilocalories per square metre per year (kcal m-2 yr-1).

sub_questions.solution: Primary productivity is the rate at which producers (autotrophs/green plants) fix solar energy and convert inorganic carbon dioxide into organic matter (biomass) through photosynthesis per unit area per unit time. It is expressed in units of grams of dry weight per square metre per year (g dry wt m-2 yr-1) or in energy units as kilocalories per square metre per year (kcal m-2 yr-1).

sub_questions.text: राजस्थान में एक स्थान की प्राथमिक उत्पादकता केरल के किसी विशिष्ट स्थान की तुलना में कम है — व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Some ecologists observed that primary productivity of a place in Rajasthan was low as compared to a particular place in Kerala. Explain why.

key_points: Rajasthan is largely arid/desert — it receives very little rainfall and has limited water availability and low soil nutrients.
Kerala is a tropical region with high rainfall, high humidity, high temperature, and rich biodiversity, all of which promote rapid photosynthesis.
Primary productivity depends on solar radiation, water availability, temperature, and nutrients — all are favourable in Kerala and limiting in Rajasthan.

sub_questions.solution: Primary productivity is limited by the availability of light, water, temperature, and soil nutrients. Rajasthan is largely an arid desert region with very low annual rainfall, high temperatures, and nutrient-poor sandy soils, which severely restrict plant growth and photosynthesis. In contrast, Kerala is a tropical region with abundant rainfall, high humidity, warm temperatures throughout the year, and fertile soils — conditions that are highly conducive to photosynthesis and dense vegetation. Therefore, the primary productivity of Rajasthan is significantly lower than that of Kerala.

key_points: Primary productivity is biomass fixed per unit area per unit time; expressed in g dry wt m-2 yr-1. Rajasthan's arid conditions limit water and nutrients; Kerala's tropical conditions support high productivity.

questions.solution: Primary productivity is the rate at which producers fix solar energy into organic matter through photosynthesis, expressed in g dry wt m-2 yr-1 or kcal m-2 yr-1. Rajasthan has low primary productivity because of its arid climate with scarce rainfall, extreme temperatures, and poor soils. Kerala has high primary productivity due to tropical conditions — heavy rainfall, high humidity, warm temperatures, and fertile soils — all favouring vigorous photosynthesis.

questions.text_english:
Study the diagram given below that shows the steps involved in the procedure of selecting transformed bacteria and answer the questions that follow:

The diagram shows: Plasmid with gene for ampicillin resistance and gene for tetracycline resistance. Foreign DNA is inserted into the tetracycline resistance gene (insertional inactivation) creating Recombinant DNA (Plasmid i). The recombinant plasmid is introduced into bacteria. Colonies derived from single bacteria grow on agar (Plate M, showing colonies 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Replica plating transfers colonies to Plate N containing agar with tetracycline and ampicillin. Colonies that grow on Plate N (with both antibiotics) are non-recombinant; colony 1 which does not grow on Plate N is the transformed (recombinant) colony.

sub_questions.text: उस निवह (कॉलोनी) को पहचानिए जो रूपांतरित हुई है । उत्तर की न्यायसंगतता सिद्ध कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify the colony that has got transformed. Justify your answer.

key_points: Colony 1 is the transformed (recombinant) colony.

Justification: It grows on Plate M (ampicillin agar) showing it has taken up the plasmid and is ampicillin-resistant, but does NOT grow on Plate N (tetracycline + ampicillin agar) because the foreign DNA was inserted into the tetracycline resistance gene, disrupting it (insertional inactivation).

sub_questions.solution: Colony 1 is the transformed (recombinant) colony. The justification is as follows: the foreign DNA of interest was cloned into the tetracycline resistance gene of the plasmid. This disrupts the tetracycline resistance gene (insertional inactivation), so the recombinant bacteria lose tetracycline resistance but retain ampicillin resistance. Colony 1 grows on Plate M (which contains only ampicillin) but fails to grow on Plate N (which contains both tetracycline and ampicillin), confirming that its tetracycline resistance gene has been disrupted by insertion of foreign DNA — making it the recombinant colony.

sub_questions.text: प्लाज़्मिड में उन स्थलों को क्या कहा जाता है जहाँ एंपिसिलिन तथा टेट्रासाइक्लीन के प्रति प्रतिरोधी जीनों का निवेशन किया जाता है ? आनुवंशिक इंजीनियरिंग में उनकी भूमिका का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: What are the sites in a plasmid called where ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes are inserted ? State their role in genetic engineering.

key_points: These sites are called selectable marker genes.
Role: They help identify and select transformed cells from non-transformed cells in genetic engineering experiments.

sub_questions.solution: The sites in a plasmid that carry antibiotic resistance genes (like ampicillin resistance and tetracycline resistance) are called selectable markers. In genetic engineering, their role is to identify and select bacteria that have successfully taken up the recombinant plasmid (transformation). Only transformed bacteria will survive on a medium containing the antibiotic corresponding to the selectable marker, while non-transformed bacteria die. This allows scientists to select successfully transformed cells efficiently from a large population of cells.

key_points: 1. Restriction endonuclease (e.g., EcoRI) — cuts DNA at specific recognition sequences.
2. DNA ligase — joins DNA fragments together.

sub_questions.solution: Two enzymes playing important roles in genetic engineering are: (1) Restriction endonuclease (such as EcoRI), which acts as a molecular scissors cutting DNA at specific palindromic sequences to produce fragments with sticky ends; and (2) DNA ligase, which acts as a molecular glue joining the cut ends of DNA fragments to form a recombinant DNA molecule.

sub_questions.text_english: State the role of β-galactosidase in insertional inactivation.

key_points: When a foreign DNA is inserted into the lacZ gene (which encodes β-galactosidase) in a vector, the enzyme is not produced, and recombinant colonies appear white on X-gal plates. Non-recombinant colonies produce functional β-galactosidase and appear blue.

sub_questions.solution: In insertional inactivation using the lacZ system, the foreign DNA of interest is inserted into the coding sequence of the lacZ gene, which encodes the enzyme β-galactosidase. When the foreign gene is inserted, it disrupts the lacZ gene, so no functional β-galactosidase is produced. On plates containing X-gal substrate, non-recombinant colonies (with intact lacZ) produce active β-galactosidase that cleaves X-gal, producing a blue colour. Recombinant colonies (with disrupted lacZ) cannot produce the enzyme and therefore remain white, making it easy to visually identify transformed recombinant bacteria.

Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.

Isn't it incredible that India's land area is only 2.4 per cent of the world's total land area whereas its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent! However, in these estimates of species, prokaryotes do not figure anywhere.

Biologists are always keen on collecting data with respect to species diversity observed in different regions of the world. The data collected based on the survey conducted for species richness of groups of mammals in three different regions of the world is shown in the bar graph given below. [Bar graph showing Region I with lowest taxonomic richness, Region II with medium richness, and Region III with highest richness of mammalian species.]

sub_questions.text: बार ग्राफ में क्षेत्र III में जातीय विविधता (समृद्धि) सर्वाधिक क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is the species richness maximum in Region III in the bar graph ?

key_points: Region III likely represents a tropical region (such as tropics/equatorial area) which has maximum solar energy, high temperatures, high rainfall, and greater habitat diversity, all of which support more species.

sub_questions.solution: Species richness is maximum in Region III because it likely represents a tropical or equatorial region. Tropical regions receive the highest solar radiation, have abundant rainfall and warm temperatures throughout the year, providing a more stable and productive environment. Greater productivity leads to more available energy and resources, which can support more species. Additionally, tropical regions have had a longer evolutionary time without major climatic disruptions, allowing for greater speciation and accumulation of biodiversity.

sub_questions.text: बार ग्राफ में क्षेत्र I में जातीय विविधता (समृद्धि) न्यूनतम क्यों है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why is the species richness minimum in Region I in the bar graph ?

key_points: Region I likely represents a polar or temperate region with harsh climate, low temperatures, limited resources, and less habitat diversity, supporting fewer species.

sub_questions.solution: Species richness is minimum in Region I because it likely represents a polar or cold temperate region with harsh climatic conditions — extreme cold, limited sunlight, low primary productivity, and seasonal resource availability. Such regions have limited energy and resources to support fewer species. Additionally, species living in cold regions face severe survival challenges, and fewer organisms have evolved adaptations to such extreme conditions compared to tropical regions.

sub_questions.text: पौधों तथा जन्तुओं की विविधता विश्व में एकसमान नहीं है यथा असमान वितरण अभिलक्षित होता है । उल्लेख कीजिए कि इस प्रकार की विविधता को क्या कहते हैं ।
sub_questions.text_english: Plants and animals do not have uniform diversity in the world but show rather uneven distribution. Mention what this kind of diversity is referred to as.

key_points: This uneven distribution of species diversity across different regions is referred to as Beta diversity or Gamma diversity (or simply species richness variation across habitats).

sub_questions.solution: The uneven distribution of plant and animal diversity across different regions of the world is referred to as Beta diversity (between-habitat diversity) or more broadly as the latitudinal gradient in species diversity. Species richness generally increases from the poles towards the tropics, and this pattern of unequal distribution of species across geographic areas is a fundamental pattern in ecology known as the latitudinal diversity gradient.

sub_questions.text: ऐसा क्यों है कि प्रोकैरियोट्स में पौधों और प्राणियों की तरह उनकी प्रजातियों की विविधता की अनुमानित संख्या नहीं होती है ? स्पष्ट कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Why is it that prokaryotes do not have an estimated number of their species diversity as seen in plants and animals ? Explain.

key_points: Prokaryotes are extremely difficult to culture and identify under laboratory conditions.
They lack morphological distinctiveness, and the biological species concept (reproductive isolation) does not apply to them since they reproduce asexually.
Most prokaryotes cannot be cultured in laboratory and their classification is difficult.

sub_questions.solution: Prokaryotes do not have an estimated number for their species diversity because they are exceptionally difficult to classify and enumerate. The traditional biological species concept — based on reproductive isolation — does not apply to prokaryotes since they reproduce asexually by binary fission and can also exchange genetic material through horizontal gene transfer across different lineages. Additionally, the vast majority of prokaryotes (estimated at over 99%) cannot be cultured under laboratory conditions, making it impossible to identify, describe, and catalogue them using classical microbiological techniques. Their extreme microscopic size and morphological simplicity further complicate the estimation of their diversity.

sub_questions.text: कोशिकाओं के उस अभिलक्षण का नाम लिखकर व्याख्या कीजिए जो प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं में तो अभिलक्षित होता है परन्तु कैंसर कोशिकाओं में लुप्त हो जाता है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Name and explain the property present in normal cells but lost in cancer cells.

key_points: The property is Contact Inhibition.
In normal cells, when cells come into contact with neighbouring cells, they stop dividing — this property is called contact inhibition.
Cancer cells lose this property and continue to divide uncontrollably, forming tumours.

sub_questions.solution: The property is Contact Inhibition. In normal cells, when a cell comes into physical contact with neighbouring cells, signals are exchanged that inhibit further cell division. This property of stopping division upon contact ensures that cells occupy only their designated space in a tissue and maintain the proper architecture. In cancer cells, this contact inhibition is completely lost due to mutations in genes regulating cell division. As a result, cancer cells continue to divide uncontrollably even when surrounded by other cells, leading to the formation of a tumour mass.

sub_questions.text: मानव की सभी प्रसामान्य कोशिकाओं में वे जीन होते हैं जो विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों में कैंसरजनी हो सकते हैं । उनका नाम लिखिए तथा बताइए कि वे कैसे उपयुर्क्त रूप में व्यवहार करते हैं ।
sub_questions.text_english: All normal human cells have genes that may become cancerous under certain conditions. Name them and explain how.

key_points: These genes are called Proto-oncogenes (or cellular oncogenes).
Under normal conditions they regulate cell growth and division. When mutated or over-expressed (becoming oncogenes), they cause uncontrolled cell proliferation leading to cancer.

sub_questions.solution: These genes are called proto-oncogenes or cellular oncogenes. Under normal conditions, proto-oncogenes code for proteins that positively regulate cell growth, division, and differentiation in a controlled manner. However, when proto-oncogenes are mutated by physical, chemical, or biological carcinogens, they can be activated into oncogenes. Oncogenes produce abnormal or overactive proteins that stimulate excessive and uncontrolled cell division, leading to the formation of cancer cells. Mutations may include point mutations, chromosomal translocations, or gene amplification.

sub_questions.text: जीवूतिपरीक्षा (बायोप्सी) तथा ऊतक विकृति (हिस्टोपैथोलॉजी)
sub_questions.text_english: Biopsy and Histopathology

key_points: In biopsy, a piece of the suspected tumour tissue is surgically removed and stained for examination under a microscope (histopathology) to detect cancerous cells by observing abnormal cell morphology, size, and arrangement.

sub_questions.solution: In biopsy, a small piece of tissue is surgically removed from the suspected tumour site. This tissue is then processed, thinly sectioned, stained, and examined under a microscope — a technique called histopathology. The pathologist looks for characteristic changes in cell morphology, such as irregular nuclei, increased mitotic figures, loss of tissue architecture, and invasion into surrounding tissues, to confirm whether the growth is malignant (cancerous) or benign.

sub_questions.text: चुंबकीय अनुनादी इमेजिंग (मैग्नेटिक रेज़ोनेंस इमेजिंग)
sub_questions.text_english: Magnetic Resonance Imaging

key_points: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to generate detailed images of soft tissues inside the body, helping to detect the location, size, and extent of tumours without using ionising radiation.

sub_questions.solution: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) uses powerful magnetic fields and radiofrequency pulses to generate high-resolution images of internal body structures, especially soft tissues. In cancer diagnosis, MRI is very useful for detecting tumours in the brain, spinal cord, breast, liver, and other organs where X-rays provide poor contrast. MRI can precisely map the location, size, shape, and extent of tumour growth and can distinguish between malignant and benign masses, helping in planning treatment strategies such as surgery or radiation therapy.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is primary effluent passed into large aeration tanks ?

key_points: To promote vigorous growth of aerobic microorganisms (bacteria and fungi) that break down organic matter in the sewage through secondary (biological) treatment, reducing the BOD of the effluent.

sub_questions.solution: Primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks to facilitate secondary (biological) treatment. Pumping air into the tanks promotes vigorous growth of aerobic microorganisms — bacteria and fungi — that decompose and mineralise the organic matter dissolved in the sewage. This biological degradation significantly reduces the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of the effluent, making it less polluting before it is discharged into natural water bodies.

sub_questions.text: निर्मित 'अवसाद' को क्या कहते हैं ? इसके महत्त्व का उल्लेख कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: What is the sediment formed, referred to as ? Mention its significance.

key_points: The sediment is called Activated Sludge.

Significance: A small portion is used as an inoculum to seed the next batch of sewage in the aeration tank; the remaining is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters where anaerobic bacteria produce biogas (methane, CO2, H2S) which can be used as an energy source.

sub_questions.solution: The sediment formed in the settling tank after secondary treatment is called Activated Sludge. Its significance is twofold: a small portion of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as an inoculum (starter culture of aerobic microorganisms) for the next batch of primary sewage. The remaining bulk of activated sludge is transferred into large anaerobic sludge digesters, where anaerobic bacteria decompose it and produce biogas consisting mainly of methane, carbon dioxide, and hydrogen sulphide. This biogas is a valuable source of energy and can be used as fuel.

sub_questions.text: उपचारित बहि:स्राव को प्राकृतिक जल स्रोतों में प्रवाहित करने से पूर्व निःसादन टैंक में अंतिम चरण की व्याख्या कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the final step in the settling tank before the treated effluent is released into water bodies.

key_points: The final step is disinfection/chlorination — the treated effluent is treated with chlorine gas or chlorine compounds to kill any remaining pathogenic microorganisms before releasing it into rivers, lakes, or the sea.

sub_questions.solution: The final step in the settling tank before the treated effluent is released into natural water bodies is disinfection. The treated effluent is passed through a disinfection chamber where it is treated with chlorine (chlorination) or other disinfectants to kill any remaining pathogenic bacteria, viruses, and other harmful microorganisms. This step ensures that the released effluent does not contaminate drinking water sources or cause waterborne diseases in the surrounding population.

sub_questions.text: विभिन्न जीव-जगतों के किन्हीं दो जीवों के नाम लिखिए जिनका आम तौर पर उपयोग जैव-उर्वरकों के रूप में किया जाता है । लिखिए कि इनमें से प्रत्येक जीव जैव-उर्वरक के रूप में कैसे कार्य करता है ।
sub_questions.text_english: Name any two organisms commonly used as biofertilisers, belonging to different kingdoms. Write how each one acts as a biofertiliser.

key_points: 1. Rhizobium (Kingdom Bacteria/Monera) — fixes atmospheric nitrogen in root nodules of leguminous plants, converting N2 into ammonia which enriches the soil.
2. Mycorrhizae (Kingdom Fungi) — fungi associated with plant roots that increase the absorptive surface for water and nutrients (especially phosphorus), enhancing plant growth.

sub_questions.solution: Two organisms from different kingdoms used as biofertilisers are: first, Rhizobium (from Kingdom Monera/Bacteria), which forms a symbiotic association with the roots of leguminous plants, living in root nodules. Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen (N2) into ammonia and other nitrogen compounds that the plant can use, and surplus fixed nitrogen also enriches the surrounding soil. Second, Mycorrhizae (from Kingdom Fungi), which form a mutualistic association with the roots of most plants. The fungal hyphae greatly increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals, especially phosphorus, from the soil, promoting better growth of plants. Mycorrhizal plants are more drought-resistant and show better overall health.

sub_questions.solution: Four inheritance patterns that deviate from Mendel's laws are: incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, and polygenic inheritance.

key_points: Incomplete dominance: F1 shows intermediate phenotype; e.g., in Antirrhinum (snapdragon), red (RR) × white (rr) → pink (Rr) in F1; F2 ratio is 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white instead of 3:1.
Codominance: Both alleles are equally expressed in heterozygote; e.g., ABO blood group — IA and IB are both expressed in AB blood group individuals (IAIB).
Multiple alleles: More than two alleles exist for a gene in a population; e.g., ABO blood group is controlled by gene I with three alleles IA, IB, and i, giving rise to four blood groups.

sub_questions.solution: Incomplete dominance: When neither allele is completely dominant, the heterozygote shows a phenotype intermediate between the two homozygotes. In Antirrhinum (dog flower or snapdragon), crossing red-flowered (RR) with white-flowered (rr) plants gives pink-flowered (Rr) offspring in F1. In F2, instead of the Mendelian 3:1 ratio, a ratio of 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white is obtained, because the single R allele cannot produce enough pigment for full red colouration. Codominance: Both alleles of a gene are simultaneously and equally expressed in the phenotype of a heterozygote. In ABO blood groups, the IA and IB alleles are codominant — a person with genotype IAIB has both A and B antigens on their red blood cells, giving AB blood group. Multiple alleles: Although a diploid individual carries only two alleles, there may be more than two allele forms of a gene in the population. ABO blood type is controlled by the gene I, which has three alleles: IA, IB, and i, producing four phenotypically distinct blood groups (A, B, AB, O) in the population.

key_points: Coding strand (3'→5' non-template strand): 5'-ATGCTGATGCGA-3'
Template strand (3'→5'): 3'-TACGACTACGCT-5'
mRNA produced: 5'-AUGCUGAUGCGA-3'
The transcription unit includes: promoter region, structural gene (coding and template strands), and terminator region.

sub_questions.solution: The transcription unit is constructed as follows — the coding strand given is: 5'-A T G C T G A T G C G A-3'. The complementary template strand (read 3'→5') is: 3'-T A C G A C T A C G C T-5'. The mRNA transcribed from the template strand would be: 5'-A U G C U G A U G C G A-3'. A properly labelled transcription unit would show: the promoter region at the 5' end (upstream of the coding sequence), the structural gene containing both strands with direction arrows, the template strand labelled as 3'→5' strand, the coding strand labelled as 5'→3' strand, and the terminator region at the 3' end.

sub_questions.text: कोडिंग रज्जुक कब टेम्पलेट रज्जुक बन जाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: When does a coding strand become a template strand ?

key_points: In a different gene on the same DNA molecule, the strand that was the coding strand for one gene may serve as the template strand for another gene, depending on the orientation of the promoter and the direction of transcription.

sub_questions.solution: A coding strand of one gene can become the template strand for another gene located on the opposite strand of the same DNA molecule. Whether a strand acts as coding or template depends on the orientation of the promoter and the direction in which RNA polymerase reads it. For a given gene, only one strand serves as the template, but for a different gene on the same chromosome, the other strand may be used as the template. Thus, the same strand can act as coding for one gene and template for another.

sub_questions.text: एक द्विकुंडली डीएनए अणु एकल रज्जुक आरएनए अणु में अनुलेखन क्यों करता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why does a double-helix DNA molecule transcribe into a single-stranded RNA molecule ?

key_points: Because RNA polymerase reads only one strand (the template strand) of the DNA double helix in the 3'→5' direction and synthesises a complementary RNA strand in the 5'→3' direction, so only one RNA strand is produced.
The other DNA strand (coding strand) is not read by RNA polymerase, so no complementary RNA is made from it during the same transcription event.

sub_questions.solution: A double-helix DNA molecule transcribes into a single-stranded RNA molecule because RNA polymerase reads only one strand of the DNA — the template strand — in a 3'→5' direction, synthesising the complementary RNA in the 5'→3' direction. The other strand (the coding strand, also called the sense strand) has the same sequence as the mRNA (with T replaced by U) and is not directly read by RNA polymerase. Since only one strand is used as the template at any given gene, only one strand of RNA is produced per transcription event, resulting in a single-stranded RNA molecule.

key_points: Non-Mendelian patterns: incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles, polygenic inheritance. OR Transcription unit from given coding strand; coding strand becomes template in different gene context; only template strand read by RNA polymerase giving single-stranded RNA.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the development of male gametophyte in an angiosperm.

key_points: The pollen grain (microspore) is the first cell of the male gametophyte.
The microspore nucleus undergoes mitosis to form a larger vegetative (tube) cell and a smaller generative cell — this is the 2-celled pollen grain stage.
The generative cell divides again (either in the pollen grain or in the pollen tube) to form two male gametes (sperms), giving the 3-celled male gametophyte.

sub_questions.solution: In angiosperms, the male gametophyte develops from the microspore (pollen grain). The microspore is haploid and its nucleus divides mitotically to produce two unequal cells: a larger vegetative cell (tube cell) and a smaller generative cell — this constitutes the two-celled stage of the male gametophyte. In most angiosperms this stage is what is shed as mature pollen. After landing on the stigma, the pollen grain germinates and the pollen tube grows down through the style, guided by chemical signals. The generative cell undergoes another mitotic division inside the pollen tube to produce two male gametes (sperms). Thus, the mature male gametophyte is three-celled: one vegetative cell (tube cell) and two male gametes. The vegetative cell ultimately degenerates after the gametes are delivered to the embryo sac.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw a diagrammatic sectional view of ovary of human female and label: Blood vessels, Primary follicle, Tertiary follicle, Ovum.

key_points: Sectional view of human ovary should show: outer germinal epithelium, connective tissue stroma, primary follicles (oocyte surrounded by single layer of follicle cells), secondary follicle, tertiary/Graafian follicle (large fluid-filled antrum containing the secondary oocyte/ovum), blood vessels in stroma, and corpus luteum.

sub_questions.solution: The sectional view of the human ovary should show an oval structure covered by a layer of germinal epithelium. Inside the stroma (connective tissue), various follicles at different stages of development are visible. Primary follicles are small structures with the primary oocyte surrounded by a single layer of granulosa cells. The tertiary (Graafian) follicle is the largest structure, showing a fluid-filled antrum containing the secondary oocyte (ovum) surrounded by cumulus oophorus cells. Blood vessels (shown as tubes with thick walls) are distributed throughout the stroma. All four structures — blood vessels, primary follicle, tertiary follicle, and ovum — should be clearly labelled.

sub_questions.text: मानव स्त्री के जीवन काल की किस अवस्था में प्राथमिक पुटकों का निर्माण होता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: At which stage of life are primary follicles formed in a human female ?

key_points: Primary follicles are formed during the foetal stage (before birth) — specifically during embryonic/foetal development, when millions of primary oocytes are formed and arrested in the prophase I of meiosis, each surrounded by follicle cells to form primary follicles.

sub_questions.solution: Primary follicles are formed during the foetal stage (before birth). During foetal development, oogonial cells in the developing ovaries multiply by mitosis and then enter meiosis I, but get arrested in the prophase I stage. Each of these primary oocytes becomes surrounded by a single layer of granulosa (follicular) cells, forming primary follicles. A female infant is therefore born with about one to two million primary follicles already present in her ovaries.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the events (both hormonal and structural) that occur at the time of ovulation till the onset of the next menstrual cycle.

key_points: At ovulation: LH surge causes rupture of Graafian follicle and release of secondary oocyte.
Post-ovulation: ruptured follicle transforms into corpus luteum under LH influence.
Corpus luteum secretes high levels of progesterone and some oestrogen, maintaining the endometrium.
If fertilisation does not occur, corpus luteum degenerates (luteolysis), progesterone levels fall, endometrium breaks down, and menstruation begins.

sub_questions.solution: At ovulation (around day 14), the LH surge triggers the rupture of the Graafian follicle and the release of the secondary oocyte into the fallopian tube. After the oocyte is released, the ruptured follicle undergoes structural changes under the influence of LH and transforms into a yellowish glandular structure called the corpus luteum. The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone and moderate amounts of oestrogen. Progesterone maintains the thickened, vascularised endometrial lining of the uterus, making it receptive for implantation if fertilisation occurs. If fertilisation does not take place, the corpus luteum degenerates into the corpus albicans around day 24–26. The decline in progesterone and oestrogen levels causes the endometrium to break down, leading to menstruation (the onset of the next menstrual cycle) around day 28.

key_points: Male gametophyte development: microspore → 2-celled pollen (vegetative + generative) → 3-celled (vegetative + 2 male gametes). OR Female reproductive cycle: LH surge → ovulation → corpus luteum → progesterone → menstruation if no fertilisation.
